Would it be feasible to implement a DIS (Downforce Increase System) where a flap on the rear wing moves up to give additional downforce? It could use the same proximity rules as DRS but change the DRS zone on the straight to a DIS zone of one sweeper or fast corner. Does anyone here have the aerodynamic knowledge to say whether this is plausible? It might help with overtakes since they are complaining so much about dirty air.
Would the opposite of DRS be feasible?

Presumably it would work, which is why a lot of people campaign for active aero as a solution to the dirty air problem. As a replacement to DRS, it seems like DRS is just the simpler solution. It sounds like it would be a lot harder to find corners that would suit the DIS being implemented, and even then the point of DRS is to get cars alongside each other for braking, which be very difficult to get mid corner. It does sound a tad more interesting though as it would leave more of the overtake down to the driver.

EDIT: Just as a sidenote, the dirty air problem is mainly that drivers' front wings have reduced load, causing them to understeer. The DIS would probably be built on the front wing rather than the rear.
Good points, I suppose it would have a very limited use.
It would still be interesting to see it tried though!
